trigger.request_payload: Develop and release QIF v0.8.5 Trust Policy Rotation and Historical Replay. Preserve superseded local trust policy revisions, express rotation reason and effective boundaries, replay historical trust decisions against a named later policy without overwriting the original decision, classify changed outcomes, and route material change or missing historical inputs to governance. Keep QIF provider-neutral and standalone; do not add live cryptographic verification, external registries, key management, UI, automatic activation, authorization, authority, or semantic-truth claims. Include schema, example, deterministic verifier, retained negative fixtures, docs, AI guidance, portable package, roadmap, AOF evidence, tag, and release.

outcome_reports.note: Released implementation candidate for QIF v0.8.5 with immutable trust-policy lineage, historical replay, deterministic governance routing, 16/16 positive and 1398/1398 negative fixture checks, portable verification, and AOF organization verification 295/295.

user_answers.question: How should improvement success be judged: which metric or end state matters most?
user_answers.answer: Success means an original trust decision remains unchanged; every policy revision has explicit predecessor, rotation reason, effective window, and status; replay names original and replay policy revisions plus frozen inputs; outcome changes are reproduced deterministically; incomplete inputs or material changes fail closed into governance; no replay rewrites history or grants authority.
